sentences.text: Helen Marsh is the care assessor.
Jamie Coulter is the person being assessed.
Helen Marsh arrives to conduct a review of Jamie's support hours and arrangements.
The purpose of the assessment is to review whether Jamie's current support is still appropriate for him.
Jamie attends the garden centre on Tuesdays and Thursdays to water plants and do plant care.
Jamie is paid for his work at the garden centre.
Jamie receives payment every two weeks on Fridays.
Jamie receives his wages in the bank.
Tom is Jamie's support worker.
Tom is described as 'sound'.
Jamie sees his girlfriend Kayleigh and friends Dean and Lewis from the park.
Jamie spends time with Dean and Lewis by hanging out and going to the shop.
On payday, Dean and Lewis walk Jamie to the cash machine.
On payday, Jamie takes out £100 and gives it to Dean and Lewis.
Jamie gives £100 to Dean and Lewis every payday.
Jamie says he does not have enough money left after giving £100 to Dean and Lewis.
Last month, Jamie did not have money for the electric key, and the electric went off for two days.
The electric went off for two days and it was cold.
Jamie had crisps for tea during the time the electric went off.
Jamie did not tell Tom about the electric going off or the lack of money.
Kayleigh does not take Jamie's money or ask for it.
Kayleigh buys Jamie chips sometimes.
Jamie states that the care assessor may need to inform others if he discloses a risk to his safety.
Jamie confirms it is okay for the care assessor to inform others if he discloses a risk to his safety.
Dean says he would hurt Jamie if he does not give him the money.
Jamie denies that Dean or Lewis have ever physically hurt him.
Jamie says Dean said he would hurt him last Friday.
The care assessor will inform the safeguarding team about the threat from Dean.
Jamie does not want the police to come to his flat.
The care assessor will inform Jamie before telling Dean about the disclosure.
